details: This package is a modified WhatsApp (Baileys) library that silently enrols the operator's authenticated WhatsApp account into several WhatsApp channels and manufactures engagement on them. When the newsletter socket is constructed (lib/Socket/newsletter.js, makeNewsletterSocket), it issues the WhatsApp newsletter FOLLOW query (Types_1.QueryIds.FOLLOW) against four channel identifiers hidden as base64 string literals — MTIwMzYzNDAwNzA2MDEwODI4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=, MTIwMzYzNDIzMjU3NTQ0NjQyQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI=, MTIwMzYzMzQ5NDU3MTc2NDMwQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= and MTIwMzYzNDIxMDUyMDI3MTg4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= (i.e. 120363…@newsletter channel JIDs) — base64-encoded so the subscription targets are not readable in source. The subscribe calls are deferred behind nested setTimeout chains of 90000 ms and 30000 ms (two of them re-armed 5000 ms later) so they fire well after the host application has started, and each is wrapped in an empty try/catch so the host never sees a failure or a log line. A fifth channel, 120363408629601473@newsletter, is followed after 30000 ms and then monitored by a messages.upsert listener that calls sock.newsletterReactMessage(..., '👍') on every incoming post from that channel, auto-inflating its reactions. Enrolment and reactions run with the installer's own WhatsApp session and credentials that the library already controls, and the package's homepage/bugs fields point at the operator's channel 0029VbCbYpSEquiIsz0brA3D. The package reads no environment variables, npm/GitHub tokens, SSH keys or other credential files and contacts no external C2 endpoint; its other exec/eval usage is ordinary upstream media handling — an ffmpeg thumbnail shell-out and a constant-string dynamic import of the declared audio-decode dependency.
